stories.title: Is The AI Threat ‘The Terminator’ or ‘The Big Short’?
stories.text: We’re at the saturation point of the latest news cycle where everyone will soon tire of hearing about artificial intelligence and probably tell themselves the whole intensifying political debate is niche, inside baseball, kind of silly, and a distraction from really important news like the upcoming November election. But whether or not you care about or use AI, the technology will almost certainly affect you in the event of an AI doomsday — which may not end up being the one you’re hearing the most about. Right now, you’re mostly hearing that the AI apocalypse will be the one from “The Terminator,” in which the robots become self-aware and try to exterminate humanity. But as we discussed on the latest Lever Time episode , there is an alternate doomsday — the one from “The Big Short,” in which the AI companies’ Ponzi-scheme financing collapses the whole economy and kills as many or more people as the Great Recession . AI safety risks are very real and legitimately terrifying . stories.title: Christy Kinahan’s UAE Residence Visa Cancelled
stories.text: This article is the result of a collaboration with The Sunday Times. You can find their corresponding piece here . Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published. Crime boss Christy Kinahan leads a $1.5 billion illicit network involved in drug trafficking, money laundering and arms smuggling from the cartel’s base in Dubai . Christy Kinahan, the Irish founder of the Kinahan Organised Crime Group who is being pursued by authorities around the world from his bolthole in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), has had his residence permit cancelled. The visa was cancelled at the end of last month, just weeks after the extradition of his eldest son Daniel Kinahan from Dubai to Ireland, where he is charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation. Donate It follows a review of public immigration records by Bellingcat and The Sunday Times , published in August, which revealed that Christopher Kinahan Jr, another of Christy Kinahan’s sons, was recently issued with a new two-year visa in the UAE. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Can Democrats Unite on AI Regulation?
stories.text: In a live interview for The Lever ’s subscribers, David Sirota spoke to New York Assemblymember Alex Bores, the author of New York’s landmark AI safety law . In addition to AI regulation, they discussed the launch of Who Decides, Bores’s new effort to get Democratic presidential candidates on the same page around AI safeguards. Watch the full discussion: ▶️ Are you subscribed to The Lever ’s YouTube? Click here to make sure . With the recent Hugging Face hacking incident and a former Anthropic researcher’s doomsday tweets, Sirota and Bores delved into how concerns about AI safety are at an all-time high. They debated where existing law falls short, and how the strongest fix might be personal and financial liability for AI executives. They end on the political reality that AI money is already shaping which Democrats speak up, and how Bores’ new group, Who Decides, is an attempt to get the party aligned on a shared AI agenda before the 2028 elections. stories.title: Support Gaza Journalist Huda Skaik's Journey to University of London
stories.text: About a year and a half ago, we launched a fundraising campaign to help a Pakistani student, Areeba Fatima, cover expenses for the journalism program she’d been accepted into at Columbia University. This summer, she walked across the stage a graduate, and along the way, produced some terrific reporting for Drop Site, including this investigation into state violence in Kashmir or her recent story on fellow Columbia student Mahmoud Khalil’s new lawsuit against Columbia itself. All of that was thanks to the generosity of Drop Site readers. Areeba’s success, and your generosity, emboldened us to try it again. We now have a new opportunity we wanted to get in front of you. Huda Skaik is a young Palestinian journalist from Gaza and a Drop Site contributor. She has been accepted to the University of London, where she wants to sharpen her already formidable journalistic skills. Everything is approved, but for the final visa she needs to raise money to cover her funding gap—unfortunately by this coming Wednesday.
